segments.text: Gumgumi checks his phone in a snowy park.
He just charged it, so it's full.
But outside, it drops almost instantly.
Tiny charge-carriers called ions make the power.
But cold makes that liquid turn thick.
Thick liquid means the ions slow down.
So the battery can't push out power as fast.
Warm it up, and the power comes back too.
Cold thickens the liquid, so power output drops.
